topics.label: Introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The opening frames the final lecture and states what students should learn about cancer treatments.

topics.label: Conventional cancer treatment
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain established ways of removing or killing cancer cells and the limitations imposed by damage to healthy tissue.

topics.label: Targeting hormone-dependent cancers
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how blocking hormone signalling can suppress cancers that remain dependent on it for growth.

topics.label: Exploiting cancer cell checkpoint defects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics show how missing cell cycle checkpoints can make cancer cells selectively vulnerable to treatment.

topics.label: PARP inhibition in BRCA-deficient cancers
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how inhibiting an additional DNA repair pathway selectively kills cells already deficient in BRCA-mediated repair.

topics.label: Oncogene addiction and targeted kinase inhibition
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics develop the strategy of identifying a cancer's driving oncogenic event and inhibiting the activated protein it depends on.

topics.label: Kinase inhibitor resistance and long-term treatment limitations
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain why kinase inhibition often becomes long-term disease control rather than a cure and how treatment must adapt to resistance.

topics.label: Antibody targeting of cancer cell surface proteins
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how antibodies recognising cancer cell surface proteins can direct therapeutic effects towards those cells.

topics.label: Immune surveillance and checkpoint blockade
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine whether endogenous T cells recognise cancer and how releasing immune checkpoints can make that recognition therapeutically effective.

topics.label: Redirecting T cells towards cancer cells
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe approaches that deliberately give T cells access to tumour targets rather than relying on naturally occurring tumour recognition.

topics.label: Treatment challenges and biomarker-guided patient selection
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the difficulty of matching heterogeneous cancers to effective, tolerable treatment and the role of biomarkers in that process.

topics.label: Cancer outcome trends, prevention and early detection
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines how prevention and earlier detection contribute to apparent improvements in cancer outcomes.

topics.label: Future treatment priorities and ethical dilemmas
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics consider how to pursue better cancer treatments when patient welfare and the success of existing therapies complicate clinical decisions and trials.
